why: Walk two sorted sequences together: sort both arrays, then let each frontend value, smallest first, take the smallest backend value it still beats. A frontend that cannot beat the smallest free backend can beat nothing, and spending a small frontend on a small backend leaves the big ones for the rest.
hints: Order does not matter, only which values pair up. Sort both arrays.
Scan frontends from small to large with a pointer j on the smallest unused backend. If frontend > backend[j], pair them and move j; otherwise this frontend is useless, skip it.
One pass over the sorted frontends: count += 1 and j += 1 whenever f > b[j]. O(n log n) for the sorts.
pitfalls: The comparison is strict: equal values do not pair.
Do not pair the largest frontend with the largest backend first; that can waste it.
constraints:
• 1 ≤ n ≤ 105; frontend and backend both have length n
  • 1 ≤ frontend[i], backend[i] ≤ 109
  • (Practice bounds; the source gives none.)
